Writing the answer…### Legal Requirement:
The law does not explicitly require the officer who first registers a case to be the same one who investigates it. In fact, the Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan) allows for flexibility in assigning roles. For example, under section 156, any officer in charge of a police station may investigate a cognizable case without the order of a Magistrate [Document 4]. Additionally, in non-cognizable cases, a police officer may investigate only with the order of a Magistrate [Document 5]. These provisions do not specify that the officer who records the FIR must also be the one who investigates the case. Therefore, the law does not mandate that these roles be combined or separated.

### What Actually Happens in Our Data:
In our case records, the roles of the officer who recorded the FIR and the officer who investigated the case are mostly NOT separated. In 68 out of 74 recorded assignment pairs (92%), the same officer both recorded the FIR and conducted the investigation. Roles are split in only 6 cases. Of these 6, 3 involve an investigating officer with no recording officer on the same case, making those pairs unresolvable rather than genuinely split [Document 6].Response generated (1199 chars)
